key_insight: Neuronal ablation produces architecture-dependent language failures: gradual decline in LSTMs, threshold-like collapse from Transformer MLP damage, and smoother decline from attention-head damage.
engineering_relevance: These failure profiles offer a computational damage-tolerance perspective for assessing AI robustness, rather than direct evidence about fracture in physical materials.
method: Systematically ablate computational units in LSTM and Transformer language models.
Apply limited fine-tuning as a proxy for compensatory plasticity.
Compare performance decline and qualitative language errors across ablation targets.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports parallel syntactic and semantic decline in damaged LSTMs, semantic substitutions and rising non-responses after MLP ablation, and reduced semantic specificity after attention-head ablation.
watch_item: Parallels to aphasia and neurodegeneration are qualitative; computational ablation and limited fine-tuning do not establish biological equivalence.
paper_title: Can Language Models Get "Aphasia" From Neuronal Ablation?
